newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Brown to stick to 2.5% inflation target.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Brown to stick to 2.5% inflation target.

text.p: Gordon Brown, the British opposition Labour Party's finance spokesman, said on Friday a Labour government would stick to an inflation target of 2.5 percent and would set monetary policy to meet it.
"What I have said is I will stick by the inflation target we have set down. We have always said we will set monetary policy in that respect," he told Reuters Financial Television.

Brown was speaking as exit polls and early results in the election suggested Labour was on its way to a landslide victory over the ruling Conservatives, with Brown likely to be the next finance minister.
Markets are focused on a monetary meeting between the finance minister and Bank of England Governor Eddie George scheduled for May 7, which could well result in a small rise in interest rates.
Brown said that, if he is confirmed in the job, he will discuss with George whether the meeting will go ahead.

"People are right to say we must avoid the inflationary pressures that could exist at this time of the economic cycle. We must also tackle the problem of social security bills which have put an additional pressure on both borrowing and taxation," he said.
